newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Shell seen reporting flat profits.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Shell seen reporting flat profits.

text.p: Oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell Group is expected to report barely changed profits when it announces its first-quarter results on Thursday.
Analysts predict net income before exceptional items to range between 1.355 billion and 1.736 billion stg compared with 1.510 billion a year ago.

The average forecast is exactly the same as last year's result. All estimates are on a current cost basis, which strips out windfall profits or losses stemming from changes in oil prices on stocks values.

Industry watchers believe Shell's upstream operations will have benefited from a higher oil price and increased production. But these positive impacts are seen largely neutralised by lower gas profitability and more pressure on refining margins.
Gas profits will be hurt by the relatively mild winter weather in the first three months of 1997 compared with an exceptionally cold first quarter last year.
Kleinwort Benson analyst Paul Spedding said temperatures were about eight percent lower than normal a year ago and some five percent milder than average so far this year.

Another analyst said Shell will also have suffered from persistent industry-wide overcapacity in refining, adding downstream margins in 1996's first quarter were relatively high compared with the rest of the year.
In the chemicals sector, results are expected to be lower compared with 1996's first quarter when input prices were still relatively subdued.
But the picture is reversed when compared with last year's final quarter, when oil prices where substantially higher than now and product prices had yet to pick up, analysts said.
